content.text: Jacks Back: Five Card Draw with Jacks or Better to open. If no one opens, the same hand is kept and played as ace-to-five lowball, so fewer deals are thrown in. Suited to three to five players.

Jacks Back is a draw poker variant that emerged from the Jacks or Better tradition in American home and club play. Five Card Draw with a pair of jacks or better required to open was the dominant form until the spread of Texas Hold'em; Jacks Back adapts that game for smaller groups by keeping the same hand in play when no one opens and switching to ace-to-five lowball, so fewer deals are thrown in. It is documented as a club and home game variant in US poker literature.
Two to six players; three to five is ideal so that more hands are played and the Lowball fallback when no one opens is used often.

Five cards each face down; first betting round requires Jacks or Better to open. If someone opens, draw and second betting round as in Five Card Draw. If no one opens, same hand becomes ace-to-five lowball with a new betting round, then draw for low, then final betting and showdown.
